has expanded CPO testing/inspection capacity, notably adding Insertion 2/3 equipment," said GF Securities analyst Alicia Xia in a Tuesday investor note. "Key components such as FAU are also progressing well, helped by improving multi‑plug/unplug yield rates. At the system level, we believe major component suppliers are already on site, enabling cleanroom‑level system integration from early Sept. We now forecast Nvidia's CPO switch shipments at 15k/16k/30k/100k for 4Q26/1Q27/2Q27/2027."

Lumentum's estimated revenue from CPO and near-packaged optics is set to accelerate dramatically year over year from 2027 to 2028, according to GF data. For 2027, Lumentum is expected to generate $427M in CPO laser revenue and $501M in NPO laser revenue. In 2028, this is forecast to expand to $750M for CPO and $2.55B for NPO.

"NVL576‑based scale‑up CPO/NPO systems are expected to begin adoption in 2H27E, with two switchboards per NVSwitch tray, each board carrying four ASICs, paired with four 3.2T OEs/ASIC," Xia noted. "We reiterate our view that CPO (QM5 + 4 OEs) and NPO (QM5 + 4 OEs on sockets) are progressing in parallel, and our view is similar with Street expectations for full NPO adoption at NVL576 launch given NPO maturity. The next to watch is Feynman, which our supply chain research indicates is also being developed in both CPO and NPO variants; packaging‑side visibility suggests CPO (QM6 with six 6.4T OEs) remains on track."
GF maintains its Buy rating on Lumentum. The financial services firm also has a Buy rating on Semtech

due to its role in the NPO scale-out, which is expected to significantly improve its earnings per share figures by 2028. It is forecast to contribute $3.03 to its EPS in 2028 after contributing $0.47 in 2027.
